newsitem.title: CHINA: China auto firm cuts prices of VW Santana again.
newsitem.headline: China auto firm cuts prices of VW Santana again.

text.p: Shanghai General Automobile Sales Co has cut the price of the Santana 2000 sedan, made by a joint venture with Germany's Volkswagen AG, for the second time in 1997, the China Business Daily said on Friday.
The car sales company had slashed retail prices of the Santana 2000 by between 11,000 yuan ($1,325) to 16,800 yuan, similar to an earlier reduction on July 1, the newspaper said.
The domestic retail price of the Santana 2000 is now 164,000 yuan to 182,000 yuan, it said.

Last year, Shanghai Volkswagen -- Volkswagen's joint venture with Shanghai Automobile Group -- produced about 250,000 cars, including 110,000 Santana 2000s, and sold 239,500 cars, official figures have shown.
Competition in China's car market is fierce, the China Securites newspaper said on Friday, with average prices down by around 15 percent by the end of 1996 compared with prices in the middle of 1995.
However, the price falls had not attracted more buyers and this was leading to huge cuts in car producers' sales and profit levels, it said.
